extracted.intended_audience: scientists, members of learned societies, and general scientific readership (geologists, chemists, naturalists, observatory staff)
extracted.subtask_description: A journal issue page containing society reports, meeting summaries, book and equipment notices, and advertisements — guidance and claims about good practice for surveys, observatories, spectroscopic work, models, and scientific apparatus. Extracts practical/quality criteria and procedural guidance embedded in news and ads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of map colours for superficial deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: The difficulty of selecting colours for superficial deposits which will suit all areas of our complex island is seen in the resemblance between 'valley gravel and rainwash' and Triassic strata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map-makers should choose colours carefully to avoid confusing superficials with older strata; note that the index may exaggerate resemblances seen on the map ('In the index, however, this resemblance is greater than in the actual map').

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological memoir content and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A geological memoir should include explanatory text, colour-printed maps (sheet explanations), an index, photographic plates illustrating important rocks, and an economic section and appendix where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page: 'Explanation of Sheet 311' includes correlation discussion and index; 'Explanation of Sheet 346' includes a 48‑page economic section and appendix, seven photographic plates illustrating important rocks, and discussion of lodes, metamorphic aureoles, and soils/subsoils. Referencing previous workers and discussing correlations (e.g., Jukes-Browne on Cretaceous correlation) is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for observatory equipment and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: An observatory should be fully equipped (ordinary and self‑recording instruments), carry out regular observations (morning and evening), preserve records, transmit readings to relevant societies, and publish results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coats Observatory example: provided standard barometer and thermometer, subsequently additional instruments; 'observations were regularly taken morning and evening. The records are preserved ... readings have been transmitted monthly to the Scottish Meteorological Society, and the results are also separately published.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Observatory public outreach / educational purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An observatory may be established or maintained with an aim to stimulate public/educational interest; it should be accessible and serve instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coats family founder hoped the establishment would 'prove a stimulus to interest the rising generation ... in the study of astronomy' and the observatory was 'opened to the public' and associated with a Philosophical Institution — implying outreach and instructional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/features for efficient laboratory extractors ('flow' extractors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extractors that keep the substance covered by solvent and provide a continuous flow of clean solvent through the substance are much more effective than Soxhlets for many purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical design points: substance kept covered by solvent; continuous flow of fresh solvent directly through material; use of condenser (Burgess's patent) and stoppered complete apparatus are presented as ways to 'greatly facilitate' extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectroscopic analysis — importance of residuary/persistent lines
rubrics_metrics.description: In spark/spark‑like spectra of solutions, the residuary or most persistent lines of an element are not necessarily the most intense; when only a small quantity is present, these residuary lines are the ones that show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should determine and tabulate the residuary/persistent lines for each element to aid detection at trace concentrations; the paper tabulates lines surviving at 1%, 0.1%, 0.01%, 0.001% of the element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation of continuous solar‑radiation/brightness studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuous study of the distribution of brightness over the surface of the sun should be organised with great care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if such studies do not furnish absolute intensities of variation, they are valuable for showing the existence and rapid occurrence of important disturbances — hence careful long‑term observational organization and consistency are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy standards for crystallographic models and teaching sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections of crystallographic models should be carefully examined with regard to their accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers/suppliers claim that all sections of the model collections 'are carefully examined as regards their accuracy' and advertise sets and new models for demonstrations (e.g., symmetry of etching figures, deduction of dodecahedron faces) — implying accuracy and pedagogical suitability are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desirable construction and quality features for Wheatstone bridges
rubrics_metrics.description: Wheatstone bridges (instruments) should be soundly constructed, accurate, perfectly insulated, with substantial lugs and large well‑fitting plugs, negligible temperature coefficient, and made of best quality materials with every care taken to ensure perfect results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplier claims serve as a checklist of expected quality attributes for precision electrical measurement apparatus (accuracy guarantee, insulation, mechanical robustness, low temperature dependence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply and preservation standards for biological specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppliers of biological material should be able to supply animals either living or 'preserved by the best methods'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marine Biological Association example lists many taxa available 'either living or preserved by the best methods' — implying best practice in preservation techniques and reliable availability are criteria for specimen suppliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement layout and billing rules for the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges and formatting rules for advertisements are specified: e.g., three lines in column, per-line rates thereafter, page-fraction rates, and special billing rules for heavy type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rule quoted: '*na first line beinc in heavy type Is charged for as Two Lines.' Orders for advertisements handled by Macmillan & Co.; detailed per-line and per-page pricing is provided on the page (rates for three lines, quarter pages, half columns, whole pages, etc.).
